content.title: Where to watch the Masters: TV channel, live stream and tee times
content.text: AUGUSTA, GEORGIA - APRIL 09: Rory McIlroy of Northern Ireland lines up a putt on the eighth green during the first round of the 2026 Masters Tournament at Augusta National Golf Club on April 09, 2026 in Augusta, Georgia. (Photo by Andrew Redington/Getty Images)Andrew Redington/Getty ImagesWhile it’s still early, defending champion Rory McIlroy has an opportunity to win back-to-back Masters titles, a feat that hasn’t happened since Tiger Woods did it in 2002.McIlroy opened his title defense in impressive fashion, shooting a 5-under 67 to share the lead with Sam Burns.Article continues below this adGet Digital Access and Stay Informed With Trusted Local News.Get Digital Access and Stay Informed With Trusted Local News.ONLY 25¢McIlroy overcame some early inconsistency to put together a composed round, while Burns leaned on excellent ball-striking to match him at the top. A group of contenders sits just behind at 3-under, including Patrick Reed, Jason Day, and Kurt Kitayama, all of whom had stretches where they threatened the lead—Reed notably carded two eagles during his round.Several big names are firmly in the mix at 2-under, including world No. 1 Scottie Scheffler, Xander Schauffele, Justin Rose, and Shane Lowry. Scheffler started hot but cooled off as conditions toughened later in the day.Overall, the leaderboard is tightly packed after Day 1, with plenty of star power near the top and a challenging course setting the stage for an intriguing second round.Here's how to keep up with Round 2 of the Masters. All times are Central: Early Round 2 Coverage: 12 p.m. to 2 p.m. (Prime Video) Round 2 Coverage: 2 p.m. to 6:30 p.m. (ESPN, Masters.com) Featured Groups & Holes: 8:15 a.m. to 6:30 p.m. (Masters.com, Paramount+, Prime Video) Article continues below this adHow many people make the cut at the Masters?According to the PGA Tour, at the Masters, only the top 50 players (including ties) after the first 36 holes advance to the weekend rounds. This rule, introduced in 2020, replaced the earlier system that also allowed players within 10 strokes of the lead to make the cut. As a result, the final two rounds usually feature just over 50 competitors.Get the hookup and your Horns Up with Longhorns coverage.April 10, 2026Marley Malenfant is a 10-year multimedia journalist who’s worked in print, digital, and broadcast. His prior work includes working in West Texas as a TV reporter for KTXS. During his time there, he covered education, sports, features, and breaking News. He’s skilled in front of the camera as well as behind it. He was a freelance writer, published in D Magazine, Dallas Morning News, SB Nation, Dallas Observer, and was a personality for “The Coach Brothers” sports radio show. Outside of journalism, he was an educator in the Dallas area. He was a 2012 Mayborn Literary Nonfiction Conference grant recipient. In 2021, he was part of the NABJ student multimedia project. He graduated with a paralegal degree from El Centro in 2023. Currently, he’s a trending news reporter for the Austin American-Statesman, covering breaking News, sports, music, and legal trends.
